主要内容: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) proposed offering reforms for Business Development Companies (BDCs) and Registered Closed-End Funds, aiming to improve access to capital and investor communications. These reforms are part of implementing provisions from the Small Business Credit Availability Act and the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief, and Consumer Protection Act. The changes would streamline registration processes, allowing eligible funds to use a short-form registration statement for selling securities. Funds would also be able to qualify as Well-Known Seasoned Issuers (WKSIs), benefiting from flexible registration and communication processes. The proposal includes new reporting and structured data requirements, as well as a modernized approach to registration fee payments for interval funds. The reforms are intended to align these funds with operating companies, enhancing transparency and investor access. The SEC has proposed reforms aimed at modernizing the offering process for Business Development Companies (BDCs) and Registered Closed-End Funds. These reforms would allow affected funds to utilize many of the communication rules currently available to operating companies, including the use of a 'free writing prospectus,' factual business information, forward-looking statements, and broker-dealer research reports. Funds would also be able to satisfy their final prospectus delivery obligations by filing the prospectus with the Commission. Interval funds would register an indefinite number of shares and pay registration fees based on net issuance, similar to mutual funds and exchange-traded funds. Structured data requirements would involve the use of Inline XBRL for registration statement information, as well as financial statement information for BDCs. Funds filing Form 24F-2 would need to submit the form in XML format. Periodic reporting requirements would include key prospectus disclosure in annual reports and management’s discussion of fund performance (MDFP). Current reporting requirements would involve filing Form 8-K for material changes to investment objectives or policies and material write-downs of significant investments. Incorporation by reference would require affected funds to make materials available on a website instead of providing copies to new purchasers. The comment period for the proposal will be open for 60 days following publication in the Federal Register.
